paras: The killing of James Burns took place on the outskirts of Sylvania, Georgia, in early August 1895, when a Black man accused of an earlier murder was shot and beaten to death by white men trying to arrest him. According to the Savannah Morning News, Burns was hit seven times and finally knocked down with a rifle after an exchange of sixteen shots with his pursuers, neither of whom was hurt. A wire version carried by papers from Virginia to South Dakota told the story as "a sensational battle between officers and a desperate criminal" in which Burns took eleven bullets.

Burns was accused of having killed another Black man at Sylvania about two years earlier "on account of jealousy about a woman" and of escaping afterward. The wire account named the dead man as Frank Bender and said Burns had been in hiding ever since.

In the Savannah account, datelined Sylvania, August 3, Constable Bob Bazemore came upon Burns near a small house just outside town the previous afternoon and coaxed one of his two pistols away from him, ostensibly to look at it. Bazemore then ordered Burns to march toward Sylvania, but Burns sprang on him, wrenched the pistol back and told him to leave, "or he would blow his head off." The constable sent to town for Sheriff Brooker, who came to the scene with Will Kemp and Julius Arnett, and when Burns saw the party approaching he ran from the house into the woods.

Kemp and Arnett followed him, with Arnett circling around a branch to cut him off. By the correspondent's account, Burns turned in a clearing and fired on Kemp, who answered with a rifle and shot him through the head with his first shot. Burns then emptied his pistols at his pursuers and grappled with Arnett until Kemp came up and "felled him with the rifle," after which he fell on his face and died within minutes. The paper counted sixteen shots, eight on each side, and said Burns had been hit seven times, five by pistol and two by rifle.
The wire version differed in setting and detail: Burns was "discovered in a swamp," a "gang of deputy sheriffs" went out to capture him, and he received eleven bullets and "died soon after."
No report of an inquest or any inquiry into the killing appears in the coverage.

The Savannah Morning News printed the fullest report on August 4 under the headline "A Desperate Fight," with the subhead "An Alleged Murderer Fires Eight Shots at the Officers." Its Sylvania correspondent called Burns "a desperate colored criminal" and "the darkey," said the earlier killing "was done in cold blood," and stressed that the bullets "whistled uncomfortably close" to the pursuers' heads. The story it told was entirely the pursuers' own, and no account from Burns's side, from Black residents of Sylvania or from the Black press appears in the coverage.

A shorter wire item, datelined Sylvania, August 7 or 8, first appeared in the Alexandria Gazette's telegraphic briefs on August 7 and in Washington, New Haven and Shenandoah papers the next day. It reached Scranton and Martinsburg by August 9 and 10 and was still running in Reynoldsville, Pennsylvania, and Elk Point, South Dakota, on August 14 and 15. Headlines such as "Eleven Bullets Killed Him" and "Shot to Death by a Posse" stressed the wounds and the posse; the wire text did not give Burns's race.

The accounts disagree on the date: the Savannah dispatch of August 3 placed the fight "yesterday afternoon about sundown," that is August 2, while the wire said "Yesterday" in an August 7 dispatch and "On Tuesday" in an August 8 version, which would put it on August 6. They also differ on the wounds (seven against eleven), the place (woods outside town against a swamp) and the men involved (Kemp and Arnett with the sheriff against a "gang of deputy sheriffs"). Written from Sylvania the day after the fight and naming the participants, the Savannah report is the closer source; the wire's shared victim and accusation indicate one killing.

reader.title: Killing of James Burns
bases: Burns was killed by armed white men who had gone with the sheriff to arrest him (A1), described in the wire as a 'gang of deputy sheriffs' and a 'posse' (A3, A5).

Burns was killed during an attempt to arrest him for an alleged murder by two men accompanying the sheriff, after (by their side's account) he fired first (A1); the wire calls them deputy sheriffs (A3). Nothing reported shows a group acting outside the law rather than an arrest party under the sheriff.

The local Savannah account (A1) and a separately worded wire dispatch (A3, A5) agree that James Burns, accused of an earlier killing at Sylvania, was shot to death by men trying to arrest him, though they differ on date and details.
